title: Jesus our mother (ch. 58–60)
hookLine: Julian speaks of the motherhood of Christ, who feeds us with himself
tomorrow: why didn't God just stop sin before it ever started?

cards: Sick on the couch, and someone keeps bringing soup you didn't ask for. They fix the blanket. They check your forehead.
Part of you wants to say, I'm fine, I've got it. Julian of Norwich looks at exactly that kind of care, the feeding, the holding, the watching, and says Jesus does all of it, and more.
She writes it calmly, without apology, as if it were plain. So why does she reach for the word mother?

teach.b: First, the claim. In chapter fifty-nine, Julian says that as truly as God is our Father, so truly God is our Mother. She doesn't drop the word Father.
She sets Mother beside it, and she gives the mother's work in a special way to Christ, the second person of the Trinity. Second, the feeding.

In chapter sixty she writes that a mother can give her child her milk, but our precious Mother Jesus can feed us with himself, and does, tenderly, in the Blessed Sacrament, which she calls the precious food of true life.
For Catholics, that points straight to the Eucharist. Third, the holding.

A mother can lay her child tenderly at her breast, she writes; Jesus can lead us into his own breast through his open side. Notice she still writes he. The motherhood is in what he does, not a change of name.
Fourth, the root. The picture has one in the Gospel itself.
In Matthew, Jesus says he longed to gather Jerusalem's children the way a hen gathers her chicks under her wings.
So the answer to why mother: because feeding and holding are what she saw him do.

how: Catholics read Julian's chapters on the motherhood of Christ alongside the Gospel image of the hen and her chicks; the feeding she describes points to receiving the Eucharist at Mass.

o: a hymn sung on Mother's Day in Julian's own parish
Julian's picture of Christ caring for us as a mother
a title Catholics give Mary as the mother of Jesus

games.q: jesus our mother — tap the pairs.

s: Julian stops calling God Father when she calls God Mother
she sets Mother beside Father: as truly the one as the other.
Julian links Jesus' feeding to the Blessed Sacrament
in chapter 60, he feeds us with himself in the Blessed Sacrament.
the hen and chicks picture comes from Julian, not the Gospels
in Matthew, Jesus himself uses it for longing to gather Jerusalem.

games.q: a friend's dad is home after surgery and turns down every offer of help: grown men don't get babied. what from Julian could you gently offer?
o: Julian says God is Mother instead of Father, so he should accept it.
Julian says suffering on your own is what makes you strong.
Julian pictures Christ himself feeding and holding us; being cared for isn't only for babies.
games.why: Julian gives the mother's work of feeding and holding to Christ, and keeps the word Father too. receiving care is part of the picture, not a failure.

practice: Let your hands rest open in your lap, palms up, the way a small child's hands lie when someone else is doing the carrying.
For the rest of the sit, don't fix or earn anything; let yourself be held, by the breath, by the quiet, and, if you pray, by God.

wordCard.voice: Jesus our mother. Julian's picture of Christ caring as a mother does: feeding us with himself, holding us close.

carryVoice: Carry this: mother Jesus, who feeds us with himself and doesn't mind the fuss. Rest well.

sources.work: Revelations of Divine Love (Julian of Norwich)
